gap: Versioned MARL policy-set registry with compatibility metadata
thesis interpretation: Generic registries and MARL policy mappings exist separately; the governed interdependent policy set remains weakly represented.

gap: Coordinated or atomic policy-set promotion and rollback
thesis interpretation: Progressive rollout and rollback exist for software, but MARL-specific mixed-version and compatibility semantics remain weakly evidenced.
Infrastructure monitoring is mature; coordination failure is rarely a first-class operational signal.
Edge fleet tooling exists, but preserving coherent multi-policy state during disconnection and partial update remains weakly evidenced.

gap: Lifecycle support for true open heterogeneous populations
thesis interpretation: Dynamic components and policy populations exist at other layers, but compatible online governance of new physical agent interfaces remains weak.
I-24 is a decisive counterexample to absence but remains one unusually mature lineage.
Flexible metadata systems exist; standardisation, enforcement and demonstrated reconstruction remain incomplete.
Generic evaluation gates exist; reusable MARL gate semantics remain domain and system dependent.

gap: Deployable package contract for policy plus control semantics
thesis interpretation: Packaging technology exists; consistent inclusion of schemas, adapters, safety and target constraints remains incomplete.

gap: Formal safety assurance as generic lifecycle primitive
thesis interpretation: Runtime assurance systems exist, but the evidence is too heterogeneous for a broad lifecycle claim.
